$comment: Record 0332: OfficeCLI parity dispositions, read by tools/officecli_capability_delta.py and tools/officecli_corpus.py (see their docstrings). Keys are fnmatch patterns; the most specific match wins (property, then element, then format part). tiers: design §13 tier by OfficeCLI element ([vocabulary]:[element]) or property ([vocabulary]:[element].[property]), or by corpus class. dispositions: planned (ref = WPn or a record id), deferred (resolves to deferred-P1/P2 by the row's tier), wontfix or out-of-scope (with a reason); keys are delta:[format]:[element][.property] or corpus:[class]. corpusScripts: the tier of each example script; P0 and v1 scripts form the v1-scope subset.

Litchi writes metadata through the `/metadata` node (records 0253, 0254) and reads it at the root; OfficeCLI writes it at the root (`set / title=...`), which the read-only root refuses. WP16 (proposed in record 0332) routes root-level metadata keys to `/metadata`

no resident process: every command opens, edits and saves the file (record 0256 D5)
the command line is parsed strictly; stray words are refused, not ignored (record 0015 D4)
OfficeCLI's documented `formula` contract: no leading `=`
